name: Bor
description: Sprawling sandstone bouldering forest near the Czech-Polish border, with over 1,000 problems across 300+ boulders.

name: Kamienna Góra
description: Quartz-sandstone bouldering summit above Pokrzywno, one of the Kłodzko Basin's most popular areas with around 200 boulders.

name: Śmietniczek
description: Sun-drenched former crystalline-limestone quarry above Wojcieszów, nicknamed the 'Polish Siurana' for its orange rock.

name: Jerzmanice
description: Krucze Skały ('Raven Rocks') - a 20m+ former sandstone quarry wall by the railway station, with around 30 crack and slab routes.

name: Sokoliki
description: Poland's oldest and most iconic granite climbing area near Jelenia Góra - rough, high-friction rock similar to the Tatras, with several hundred routes.

name: Podlesice (Góra Zborów)
description: Along with neighboring Rzędkowice, one of two villages that call themselves Poland's rock-climbing capital - a limestone ridge crowned by the Zborów tower with routes across every grade.

name: Morsko
description: One of the busiest, most concentrated sport-climbing crags in the Polish Jura, known for steep pocketed limestone and hard test-pieces.

name: Rzędkowice
description: One of the most popular areas of the North Jura, with close to 500 well-bolted routes up to 30m across a maze of towers - popular with beginners and families.

name: Dolina Będkowska
description: Limestone valley 25km from Kraków with around 70 routes, home to Sokolica - the tallest limestone wall in the Jura at up to 80m and one of the few spots in the region with true multi-pitch climbing.

name: Mirów
description: Limestone crags beneath the ruins of Mirów Castle, spread across eight rock towers; Turnia Kukuczki is the most popular, with 39 routes up to 20m.

name: Toczek
description: Sandstone crag in the Góry Stołowe (Table Mountains) National Park, developed under a formal access agreement with the local forest district - named formations include Skała Budda and Bambułka 2.

name: Adamów
description: Bouldering area in the Skały pod Adamowem nature reserve, with around 200 problems mostly 5A-6C on slabby sandstone with good landings. Best from autumn through mild winter.

name: Weißenstein
description: The single most popular crag in the Frankenjura - around 50 routes from UIAA 2 to 9+, from short bouldery lines to the famous overhanging bulge on the right.

name: Krottenseer Turm
description: A freestanding limestone tower near Hersbruck, home to Wolfgang Güllich's 'Wallstreet' - the world's first 5.14b - alongside 50+ other routes from easy to extreme.

name: Waldkopf
description: Historic crag near Egloffstein, home to Wolfgang Güllich's 'Action Directe' - the world's first 9a and a landmark in sport-climbing history.

name: Obertrubach
description: A core Frankenjura area along the Trubach valley, with a dense cluster of limestone crags from easy to hard.

name: Houbirg
description: A large limestone dome near Happurg with a more adventurous, multi-pitch character than the Frankenjura's typical single-pitch sport crags.
